status_summary: ONDCP's drug policy priorities released on 2025-04-03 list reducing overdose fatalities with a focus on fentanyl first of six, followed by supply chain, border, prevention, treatment and research, without stating a ranking. The HALT Fentanyl Act (Public Law 119-26) was approved on 2025-07-16, and Executive Order 14367 (90 FR 59365), signed 2025-12-15, designated illicit fentanyl and core precursors weapons of mass destruction. The 2026 National Drug Control Strategy, released 2026-05-04, ranks no goals, calls supply and demand efforts equally important, emphasizes illicit fentanyl as a central lethal threat and sets a goal of accelerating the decline in overdose deaths; its fact sheet lists border interdiction first and overdose response last. No document was found describing the Director's consultation with border officials.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14157 (90 FR 8439, published 2025-01-29) directs a State Department recommendation within 14 days on designating covered cartels as foreign terrorist organizations or specially designated global terrorists.
ONDCP released the administration's six drug policy priorities, led by reducing overdose deaths with a focus on fentanyl.
The HALT Fentanyl Act became Public Law 119-26, placing fentanyl-related substances in Schedule I as a class.
Executive Order 14367 designated illicit fentanyl and core precursors as weapons of mass destruction and assigned enforcement tasks to Justice, State, Treasury, War and Homeland Security.
The Senate confirmed Sara Carter as ONDCP Director by a 52 to 48 vote.

A presidential document dated this day describes the Americas Counter Cartel Coalition, set up by the Secretary of War as a pledge by military leaders and representatives of 17 countries, with goals including dismantling cartels designated as foreign terrorist organizations.

ONDCP released the 2026 National Drug Control Strategy; the strategy ranks no goals, treats supply and demand efforts as equally important, emphasizes illicit fentanyl and sets a goal of accelerating the decline in overdose deaths, while its fact sheet opens with border interdiction and cartels and places overdose response last.

State published the foreign terrorist organization designation of the Juarez Cartel and Los Viagras under section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act, effective on publication (signed 2026-07-02).

ONDCP releases a Drug Threat Notice on fentanyl analogues (carfentanil, fluorofentanyl, methylfentanyl), citing CDC estimates of at least 12,500 deaths since 2023; the release page states no legal effect.

title: Make fentanyl and overdoses the top drug policy priority; consult border officials
uncertainties: The 2026 strategy PDF was read in review only in part (through about Chapter 5; Appendices A, B and D, including the border strategies appendix and performance goals, were not visible), so a passage on the Director consulting border enforcement officials cannot be ruled out; the visible text mentions only views solicited from National Drug Control Program agencies and law enforcement organizations. CRS report R48859 was not read. Overdose death trends were not examined beyond the figures the strategy cites. The cartel designation notices of 2026 and Executive Order 14157 are context on supply reduction. The progress figure is an inference: the 2025 priorities statement matches the recommendation directly, while the 2026 strategy balances supply and demand without naming a top priority. The Drug Threat Notice release page of 2026-09-15 states no legal consequence; the linked PDF was not read.
